coverage: All twenty-nine scenes in both original-en and modern-en: named cast, speaking and stage roles, scene-local lords, ladies and messengers, the British and Roman figures of the tribute argument, and the classical figures named in the play.

entities.name: Imogen
entities.body: Cymbeline’s daughter, who has married Posthumus against her father’s will.

snapshots.body: Cymbeline’s daughter, leaving Britain in a boy’s clothes at Pisanio’s advice.
Cymbeline’s daughter, travelling as a boy under the name Fidele.
Cymbeline’s daughter, known again at her father’s court.

entities.name: Posthumus Leonatus
entities.body: A gentleman raised at Cymbeline’s court and married to Imogen; his surname is Leonatus.

snapshots.body: Imogen’s husband, come back to Britain in the Roman army but meaning to fight for Britain as a peasant.
Imogen’s husband, giving himself out as a Roman so as to be taken prisoner.

entities.name: Cymbeline
entities.body: The King of Britain, Imogen’s father.

entities.name: The Queen
entities.body: Cymbeline’s second wife and Cloten’s mother; the play gives her no name.

entities.name: Cloten
entities.body: The Queen’s son by an earlier husband, and Cymbeline’s stepson.

entities.name: Iachimo
entities.body: An Italian gentleman at Philario’s house in Rome, brother to the Duke of Siena.

entities.name: Pisanio
entities.body: Posthumus’s servant, left behind in Britain in Imogen’s household.

entities.name: Belarius
entities.body: An old man living in a cave in the Welsh mountains, who goes by the name Morgan.

snapshots.body: The banished lord Belarius, who stole Cymbeline’s two sons in revenge and has raised them in Wales under the name Morgan.

entities.name: Guiderius
entities.body: A young man raised in the Welsh cave, called Polydore by the old man who brought him up.

snapshots.body: Cymbeline’s elder son, stolen in infancy and raised in Wales as Polydore.

entities.name: Arviragus
entities.body: The younger of the two young men raised in the Welsh cave, called Cadwal.

snapshots.body: Cymbeline’s younger son, stolen in infancy and raised in Wales as Cadwal.

entities.name: Caius Lucius
entities.body: The Roman general sent as ambassador to Britain to demand the tribute.

entities.name: Philario
entities.body: Posthumus’s host in Rome, a friend of his father’s.

entities.name: Cornelius
entities.body: A physician at Cymbeline’s court.

entities.name: The Soothsayer
entities.body: The Roman soothsayer who reads the omens for Lucius; Lucius calls him Philarmonus.

entities.name: Sicilius Leonatus
entities.body: Posthumus’s father, who fought beside Cassibelan and died before his son was born; he appears in the prison as an apparition.

entities.name: Jupiter
entities.body: The king of the gods, also called Jove and the Thunderer, who descends in the prison.

entities.name: The First Lord
entities.body: A lord attending Cloten, who flatters him.

entities.name: The Second Lord
entities.body: A lord attending Cloten, who mocks him in asides.

entities.name: Helen
entities.body: The lady who attends Imogen; Imogen calls her by name at her bedside.

entities.name: The Queen’s lady
entities.body: One of the ladies gathering flowers for the Queen.

entities.name: The lord at court
entities.body: A lord attending Cymbeline as the Roman war begins.

entities.name: The lord in the field
entities.body: The British lord who runs from the battle and meets Posthumus.

entities.name: The Gaoler
entities.body: The gaoler who keeps Posthumus in the British prison and talks with him about dying.

entities.name: The Second Gaoler
entities.body: The second gaoler in the British prison, who calls Posthumus out.

entities.name: The Second Senator
entities.body: A Roman senator who assents to the commission.

entities.name: The attendant
entities.body: An attendant at Cymbeline’s court.

entities.name: The Roman captain
entities.body: The captain who takes the disguised Imogen into Lucius’s service.

entities.name: The First Captain
entities.body: A British captain in the field after the battle.

entities.name: The Second Captain
entities.body: A British captain in the field after the battle.

entities.name: The Tribune
entities.body: A Roman tribune ordered to levy troops for Britain.

entities.name: The First Senator
entities.body: A Roman senator who reads out the Senate’s commission.

entities.name: The messenger at court
entities.body: The messenger who announces the Roman ambassadors.

entities.name: The messenger at the prison
entities.body: The messenger who calls Posthumus before the King.

entities.name: The First Gentleman
entities.body: A gentleman of Cymbeline’s court who explains the marriage to a newcomer.

entities.name: The Second Gentleman
entities.body: The gentleman to whom the court’s story is explained.

entities.name: The Frenchman
entities.body: A French gentleman at Philario’s house who has met Posthumus before in Orleans.

entities.name: The Dutchman
entities.body: A Dutch gentleman among the company at Philario’s house.

entities.name: The Spaniard
entities.body: A Spanish gentleman among the company at Philario’s house.

entities.name: Posthumus’s mother
entities.body: Posthumus’s mother, who died in giving birth to him; she appears in the prison as an apparition.

entities.name: The First Brother
entities.body: The elder of Posthumus’s two brothers, killed in the wars; he appears in the prison as an apparition.

entities.name: The Second Brother
entities.body: The younger of Posthumus’s two brothers, killed in the wars; he appears in the prison as an apparition.

entities.name: The lords
entities.body: The lords of Cymbeline’s court.

entities.name: The ladies
entities.body: The ladies attending the Queen.

entities.name: The attendants
entities.body: The attendants at Cymbeline’s court.

entities.name: The musicians
entities.body: The musicians Cloten brings to play beneath Imogen’s window.

entities.name: The Roman senators
entities.body: The senators who commission the levy for Britain.

entities.name: The Roman tribunes
entities.body: The tribunes given the Senate’s commission.

entities.name: The gaolers
entities.body: The gaolers who bring Posthumus in irons.

entities.name: The captains
entities.body: The captains of the two armies.

entities.name: The Leonati
entities.body: Posthumus’s family, the Leonati of Britain.

entities.name: Augustus Caesar
entities.body: The Roman emperor who demands the tribute from Britain.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman general who conquered Britain in Cassibelan’s time.

entities.name: Cassibelan
entities.body: The British king who resisted Julius Caesar; Cymbeline’s uncle.

entities.name: Tenantius
entities.body: The British king from whom Sicilius had his titles; Cymbeline’s father.

entities.name: Mulmutius
entities.body: The ancestor who ordained Britain’s laws and first wore the golden crown.

entities.name: Lud
entities.body: The British king whose town the play calls Lud’s Town.

entities.name: Euriphile
entities.body: The nurse who stole Cymbeline’s sons and whom the boys take for their mother.

entities.name: Dorothy
entities.body: One of Imogen’s women, named once when Imogen sends word to her.

entities.name: The Duke of Siena
entities.body: Iachimo’s brother, named only as the leader whose men serve under Lucius.

entities.name: Richard du Champ
entities.body: A name Imogen invents on the spot for the master she claims to have lost; no such man exists in the play.

entities.name: Cleopatra
entities.body: The Egyptian queen worked into the tapestry in Imogen’s bedchamber, meeting Antony on the Cydnus.

entities.name: Tarquin
entities.body: The Roman who crept upon the sleeping Lucrece, whom Iachimo names as he steps from the trunk.

entities.name: Sinon
entities.body: The Greek whose false weeping opened Troy to the wooden horse.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: The Trojan whose faithlessness to Dido made honest men doubted.

entities.name: Hecuba
entities.body: The queen of Troy, whose curses on the Greeks Imogen calls down on Pisanio.

entities.name: Thersites
entities.body: The most contemptible of the Greeks at Troy, whose dead body Guiderius says is as good as Ajax’s.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: The great Greek warrior at Troy, set against Thersites in Guiderius’s comparison.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The strongest of the Greek heroes, who could not knock brains out of a head that had none.

entities.name: Philomel
entities.body: The woman of the Ovid story Imogen has been reading, turned into a nightingale.

entities.name: Tereus
entities.body: The king of the same story, who violated Philomel.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The chaste goddess and huntress, whose bathing is carved on Imogen’s chimneypiece.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The queen of the gods.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The goddess of love, also called Cytherea.

entities.name: Minerva
entities.body: The goddess of wisdom, set beside Venus in Iachimo’s praise.

entities.name: Lucina
entities.body: The goddess of childbirth, who failed Posthumus’s mother.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The god of war.

entities.name: Saturn
entities.body: The cold planet-god, set against the fire of Iachimo’s account.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The god of the sea, whose park Britain is called.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: The sun god, whose horses drink at the springs in the song.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The god of love.

entities.name: Titan
entities.body: The sun, under his other name.
